AltRA-Test An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators

Abstract

As LLM judges increasingly replace human annotators, a reliable statistical test is needed to decide whether an LLM judge can actually replace humans. The Alternative Annotator Test (Alt-Test; Calderon et al., 2025) was a first step, designed for dense settings in which the same annotators label every item, whereas in many large-scale settings different items have different annotators. AltRA-Test, the Alternative Annotator Test with Resampled Annotations, works in all annotation settings without requiring shared annotators, and needs only three human annotations per item, often for about 100 items. It replaces one human annotation per item with the LLM annotation and tests whether inter-annotator agreement stays as high as among the humans alone, that is, whether the LLM preserves the signal the annotators share. In simulations, where the better annotator is known, AltRA-Test makes more correct replacement decisions than existing baselines. On real data, covering 18 LLMs, 5 prompting techniques and 20 datasets across text, image, audio and video, LLMs pass in about half of the setups, depending mainly on the task.

Authors

Nagham Omar
Faculty of Data and Decision Sciences
Technion

Nagham Omar is a master's student in the Faculty of Data and Decision Sciences at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, advised by Prof. Avigdor Gal. Her research spans ordinal alignment problems in machine learning, LLMs as judges, and active learning.

Rotem Dror
Faculty of Computer and Information Science
University of Haifa

Dr. Dror is a faculty member at the University of Haifa. Her research is on drawing reliable conclusions from empirical evidence in NLP: statistically sound model evaluation, measuring the quality of data annotations, and deciding when LLMs can stand in for human judgment. She was a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Pennsylvania with Prof. Dan Roth and received her PhD from the Technion, advised by Prof. Roi Reichart.

Google Research
Avigdor Gal
Faculty of Data and Decision Sciences
Technion

Prof. Gal's research focuses on effective methods of integrating data from multiple and diverse sources under conditions of uncertainty. With close to 200 publications in leading journals and conferences in the areas of databases and AI, he is a recipient of multiple best paper and test of time awards.

Roi Reichart
Faculty of Data and Decision Sciences
Technion

Prof. Reichart is a Professor and Vice Dean for IT at the Faculty of Data and Decision Sciences at the Technion, an affiliated lecturer at the Centre for Human-Inspired Artificial Intelligence at the University of Cambridge, and an ELLIS fellow. He was Co-Editor-in-Chief of TACL from 2022 to 2026 and is a PC chair of EACL 2027.

Nitay Calderon
Google Research

Dr. Calderon is a Research Scientist at Google Research in Tel Aviv. He completed his PhD in the Faculty of Data and Decision Sciences at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, advised by Prof. Roi Reichart, as a Clore fellow. His research spans NLP, causal inference, concept-based explainability and domain adaptation.
